cards.explanation: The answer is that God is with Abraham in all he does. Abimelech, king of Gerar (Genesis 20:2), says it together with Phicol, the commander of his army: "God is with you in all that you do." (Genesis 21:22) They could have opened with anything. They led with God. Nobody is complimenting Abraham's cookie recipe here, friends.

The word is "falsely." Abimelech asks Abraham to swear that he will not "deal falsely" with him or his children or descendants. (Genesis 21:23) He wants honesty to last past his own lifetime. I think that's a king who plans ahead, because I can't even plan past lunch.
The answer is True! Abraham answers, "I swear it." (Genesis 21:24) That's all he says. Three words, and the oath is agreed. I wish my answers to "what do you want for dinner" were that short.

The complaint is about a well the king's servants seized. Abraham complained to Abimelech "…about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized…" (Genesis 21:25) The servants took the well, and Abraham brought his complaint to the king. Picture someone eating the last cookie you were saving, and you're the one walking up to the boss about it. Abraham just took it straight to the top.

The answer is True. Abimelech says, "I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today." (Genesis 21:26) Notice he says two things: he doesn't know who did it, and Abraham hadn't told him. That's a lot of "I don't know" packed into one answer.

The word is "covenant." Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and cattle, "…and the two men made a covenant." (Genesis 21:27) A covenant is a solemn agreement between two parties. The text puts the gift and the covenant side by side in one verse. I'd say that beats a handshake and a smile.

Abraham says the seven ewe lambs are his witness that he dug the well. He says, "You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well." (Genesis 21:30) Seven lambs, and every one of them is a witness. Abimelech asked a simple question and got a simple answer. I've had cookie orders with less paperwork than this well.

The place is called Beersheba. The text says the place "…was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath." (Genesis 21:31) The name comes from what happened right on that spot. It's like a bakery named after the first batch that ever came out of its oven. You hear the name, and you know the story.

The answer is True. "After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines." (Genesis 21:32) The covenant comes first, and then they go. The very next verse has Abraham planting a tamarisk tree at Beersheba. (Genesis 21:33) So the story keeps going, friends.

Besides planting the tree, Abraham calls on the name of the LORD. At Beersheba, Abraham planted a tamarisk tree, "…and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God." (Genesis 21:33) He plants, and then he prays. I think that's a good order for any day.
The answer is False. The text says, "…Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for a long time." (Genesis 21:34) He's not rushing off, and he settles in for a long stay.
